question_text:
Using the ionic radii in  table 3.4 , compute the theoretical density of CsCl. (Hint: Use a modification of $$
a=\frac{4 R}{\sqrt{3}}
$$.)

Refer to  table 3.4 :
 table 3.4 
Ionic Radii for Several Cations and Anions for a Coordination Number of 6
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline Cation & Ionic Radius (nm) & Anion & Ionic Radius (nm) \\
\hline $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ & 0.053 & $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$ & 0.196 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}$ & 0.136 & $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ & 0.181 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ & 0.100 & $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ & 0.133 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Cs}^{+}$ & 0.170 & $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ & 0.220 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ & 0.077 & $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ & 0.140 \\
\hline $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ & 0.069 & $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ & 0.184 \\
\hline $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ & 0.138 & & \\
\hline $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$ & 0.072 & & \\
\hline $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ & 0.067 & & \\
\hline $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ & 0.102 & & \\
\hline $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ & 0.069 & & \\
\hline $\mathrm{Si}^{4+}$ & 0.040 & & \\
\hline $\mathrm{Ti}^{4+}$ & 0.061 & & \\
\hline
\end{tabular}The unit of the answer is g/cm^3.
response:
## Solution

**Step 1 — Lattice parameter:**

The CsCl structure has ions touching along the body diagonal. From corner to body center ($\tfrac{a\sqrt{3}}{2}$), the two ions touch:

$$a = \frac{2(R_{\text{Cs}^+} + R_{\text{Cl}^-})}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{2(0.170 + 0.181)}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{0.702}{\sqrt{3}} = 0.4053 \text{ nm}$$

**Step 2 — Unit cell volume:**

$$V_c = a^3 = (0.4053 \times 10^{-7} \text{ cm})^3 = 6.658 \times 10^{-23} \text{ cm}^3$$

**Step 3 — Theoretical density:**

The CsCl unit cell contains $n = 1$ formula unit (1 Cs⁺ at 8 corners × ⅛, plus 1 Cl⁻ at body center). With $A_{\text{CsCl}} = 132.91 + 35.45 = 168.36$ g/mol:

$$\rho = \frac{n A}{V_c N_A} = \frac{(1)(168.36)}{(6.658 \times 10^{-23})(6.022 \times 10^{23})} = 4.20 \text{ g/cm}^3$$

$$\boxed{4.20}$$
